Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice N S Sanjay Gowda
 Oral Judgment
1. The claimants are in appeal challenging the dismissal of their claim petition.

2. The Tribunal has dismissed the claim petitions essentially on the ground that the charge sheet was laid against the rider of the motorcycle i.e., Mahendra Reddy (one of the claimants) and therefore, they cannot claim compensation.
3. The accident occurred between a two wheeler and another motorcycle, which was insured by the insurer.

The pillion rider as well as the rider i.e., the claimants categorically contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the other motorcycle and also they adduced their oral evidence to that effect.

4. The rider of the other motorcycle, however, did not choose to enter appearance and the insurer sought to rely upon the charge sheet to contend that the negligence was entirely on the part of the rider of the motorcycle i.e., one of the claimants.
In my view, this approach of the insurer would be incorrect.

If the negligence is alleged against NC: 2024:KHC:45881 the rider of the motorcycle i.e.,
one of the claimants, the evidence produced by the rider of the motorcycle i.e., the claimant would have to be rebutted by the evidence of the rider of the other motorcycle.
In the absence of any such rebuttal evidence, the assertion of the claimants would have to be upheld.
5. In this view of the matter, the dismissal of the claim petition cannot be accepted and the finding with regard to attribution of negligence is set aside.

6. Since the Tribunal has not assessed any compensation and since the claimants, though claimed to have suffered fractures, have not examined any Doctors to establish the same, I am of the view that it would be appropriate to remand the matter to the Tribunal to assess the compensation.
7. It would be open to the claimants to adduce evidence to establish the extent of disability suffered by them due to the accident.

It would also be open to the insurer to adduce evidence in that regard.
8.
The parties who are represented by their respective counsel shall appear before the Tribunal on 17.12.2024.
The appeals are accordingly allowed and remanded to the Tribunal.
